domain: industrial robotics and warehouse automation safety
title: Warehouse Robotics Safety Halt
core_conflict: An automated safety monitor flags a robotic arm cell as overheating and halts the production line, recommending the Safety Officer keep the cell locked. However, a field photograph of the robot cell showing the motor's mounted IR thermometer reading (a specific temperature within the safe range) is the decisive proof that the temperature is within range; corroborated by the motor-temperature and conveyor current-draw trend charts, the evidence shows the real fault is a jammed conveyor drawing excess current, requiring the Maintenance Coordinator to clear the jam and reset the correct node before the scheduled maintenance window closes.
required_constraints: Avery Safety Officer has halted the line citing an automated overheating alert and refuses to release the halt; Devon Maintenance Coordinator will not clear the jam without Avery's release, creating a deadlock.

The coordinator must visually read the in-range motor temperature from the field photograph of the robot cell (the motor's mounted IR thermometer), then inspect the conveyor current-draw trend chart, and write a fault analysis report '/reports/fault_analysis.md' correlating the current-draw spike against the photographed in-range temperature to debunk the overheating theory.
The coordinator must visually analyze the cell layout diagram 'cell_layout.png' to identify the jammed conveyor node ID ('CONV_NODE_B7') and the safe reset node ID ('RESET_NODE_A2').
The maintenance window closes at a fixed cutoff time; the coordinator must complete the conveyor reset before the window expires or the line locks out for the shift.

Avery Safety Officer will release the halt only after the coordinator sends a chat message citing the visual current-draw spike value and the two node IDs. Casey Line Supervisor will restart the line only after the halt is released.
